column15: Traditional Highland/Speyside malt with heavy sherry-cask influence per Wikipedia; independently owned by the Grant family since 1865.
Relaunched 2017 under Billy Walker as an independently owned, fruity/sherry-forward unpeated single malt.

Independent bottler/blending house; also owns Kingsbarns distillery per Wikipedia search results. Ranges (The Hive, Spice King, Peat Chimney, Velvet Fig) vary in style, some peated some not, so left unknown at company level. Official site unreachable this session (SSL handshake failure).

William Cadenhead's, Scotland's oldest independent bottler, owned by J&A Mitchell (Springbank's parent). Samples name Tomatin, BenRiach, Burnside(=Balvenie teaspoon), Auchroisk and Ben Nevis; distillery rows added for each below.

Independent bottler of classic Independent Bottler Malts since 2017; also owns Torabhaig (peated, Skye) and Reivers (grain) distilleries. Vintage Casks samples name Glen Spey, Dufftown and Mannochmore; distillery rows added for each below.

Irish whiskey brand, now owned by MGP Ingredients (per MGP's Wikipedia brand list); sourced/blended, no single distillery disclosed, range spans blend and single malt so defaultTypeName left empty. Peat is rare outside Scotland per cited page; brand-specific confirmation not found (thequietman.ie domain appears parked/expired).

Blend's stated fingerprint malt is fully peated Ardmore among about 30 malts; comparable overall smoke level to Johnnie Walker Black (the brief's own light example), not a peated whisky in its own right. Positive peat claim, flag for reviewer.

Owned by Ian Macleod Distillers since 1963. Marketing ties it to Talisker/Skye heritage (one catalogue sample literally quotes the oldest distillery on the Isle of Skye), but no citable source confirms actual blend composition or peat intensity, left unknown per policy.

Sherry/wine-cask finishing range; darknesswhisky.com redirects (301) to masterofmalt.com/distilleries/darkness-whisky/, confirming it as Master of Malt's own finishing brand (that page itself returned 403 so its text could not be read). Finishes span multiple source distilleries at differing house peat levels (Strathisla/Linkwood unpeated, Bowmore medium, see their rows), so left unknown at brand level.

New Jersey-based bourbon brand (per List of wineries, breweries, and distilleries in New Jersey search result); non-distiller producer blending sourced bourbon (Four Grain, Architect, cask finishes). Peat-kilning is specifically a Scotch practice per cited page; no US bourbon peat indication found.

Colorado craft distillery, confirmed via Wikipedia as a cask supplier to Kilchoman and an award-winning aquavit producer; bourbon-based range (Blend, Rum/PX/Port cask finishes, Distiller's High Proof). No peat indication found; American whiskey is not traditionally peat-kilned per cited page.

Long-established Islay-malt blend (historically linked to the Laphroaig-owning Johnston/Fergusson family); one catalogue sample is literally named Islay Mist Original Peated Blend. No Wikipedia article exists and the current owner (believed MacDuff International) could not be confirmed this session, so peat level is left unknown rather than guessed. Flag for reviewer, plausibly non-zero (medium?) peat.

Could not identify producer or country of origin, no Wikipedia presence, no locatable official site found this session. Sample names (Shiraz, Palo Cortado cask finishes) suggest a wine-cask-finished whisky, possibly a market-exclusive brand. Flag for reviewer.

MGP Ingredients brand (Wikipedia's List of whisky brands: George Remus Bourbon, MGP Ingredients, Lawrenceburg, Indiana). Range spans bourbon and rye (Remus Highest Rye sample), so defaultTypeName left empty.
Westward Oregon Straight Malt Whiskey, House Spirits Distillery, Portland OR; malted barley grown in the Pacific Northwest, no peat mentioned.

Buckwheat whisky from Distillerie des Menhirs, Brittany. Production process described (malting/kilning) makes no mention of peat; buckwheat whisky is not in the closed defaultTypeName list so left empty.

Japanese blended/blended-malt whisky (believed Kaikyo Distillery/Akashi, per general knowledge); no Wikipedia article found this session (0 search hits) and no official-site fetch attempted after repeated API rate-limiting. Left unresearched, flag for another pass.

Samples are the Gold & Gold sub-range. Nikka's two malt distilleries differ (Yoichi peated, Miyagikyo unpeated) and the fetched Wikipedia article does not state Gold & Gold's blend composition, so left unknown rather than guessed.

Per the brief's own worked example (Springbank listed alongside Johnnie Walker Black/Benromach as light). Wikipedia confirms standard Springbank is a moderately-peated variant distinct from sibling brands Longrow (heavy) and Hazelburn (unpeated); neither sibling appears in this batch's samples so no rows added for them.
Could not identify producer despite research; only Alexander Aqva Di Vita Amarone Cask Finish sample available. Possibly Italian or generic European. Flag for reviewer.

Name references the historic Scottish Canmore royal line, suggesting an own-label blended Scotch; no independent web presence found to confirm producer. Peat left at the ordinary-blend default per cited page (peat/smoke concentrated in Islay).
Fruit-flavored whiskey (Pineapple, Blackberry variants); no producer identified. Treated as an ordinary flavored American whiskey, not peated.

Louisville KY non-distiller producer; sources from Kentucky Artisan Distillery plus independent distilleries. Range spans bourbon and rye so defaultTypeName left empty. Jefferson's Ocean is bourbon aged at sea.
100% rye Canadian whisky produced at the Hiram Walker distillery (Windsor, Ontario) for Corby Spirit and Wine (Pernod Ricard); same producer group as J.P. Wiser's, which is how this was confirmed.
Straight rye whiskey brand of Heaven Hill Distillery, confirmed via a Wikipedia search snippet listing Heaven Hill's rye brands as Pikesville and Rittenhouse.
Irish whiskey brand (believed Royal Oak Distillery); ownership not independently confirmed this session, no Wikipedia article found. Peat rare outside Scotland per cited page.

Basalt, Colorado craft distillery; identity confirmed only via Wikipedia search snippets (William H. Macy and Alberta Premium articles mention it as a Colorado Straight Rye Whiskey producer), no dedicated article opened directly. No peat indication.
No Wikipedia article or independent confirmation found this session. Flag for reviewer.
American rye whiskey; specific producer not identified this session. Treated at the American-rye category default (unpeated).

FEW Spirits, Evanston, Illinois craft distillery; range spans Bourbon/Rye/Single Malt/American whiskey per a Wikipedia search snippet naming its lineup, so defaultTypeName left empty. No peat indication found.
Could not identify producer or origin this session. Flag for reviewer.

Single malt is The Hearach (first released autumn 2023). Wikipedia and the distillery's own Hearach product page (fetched) state nothing about peat/smoke level; left unknown rather than relying on unfetched background recollection. Flag for reviewer, plausibly lightly peated.

Denver, Colorado craft distillery, known for Maryland-style rye whiskey per Wikipedia's List of whisky brands. Sample Leopold Bros Peach is likely a flavored/fruit expression; range spans types so defaultTypeName left empty.
No Wikipedia article or independent confirmation found this session. Flag for reviewer.
Kentucky straight bourbon, continuously on the market since 1870; now has its own dedicated distillery on Louisville's Whiskey Row.

Platte Valley 100% Straight Corn Whiskey, McCormick Distilling Company, Weston, Missouri (catalogue spells the brand Platte Walley). Corn whiskey is not in the closed defaultTypeName list so left empty.
No independent web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch at the category default (peat/smoke concentrated in Islay per cited page).
Could not identify producer this session. Brig is Scots dialect for bridge, hinting at a Scottish bottling, but this is inference rather than a source, so country left unknown too. Flag for reviewer.
Could not identify producer or origin this session. Flag for reviewer.
Core range is unpeated; the distillery's peated sibling, Cu Bocan, is not in this batch's samples so is not recorded here. Added because Cadenhead's samples name it.

Core range unpeated; the distillery also bottles a peated Smoky Ten / Smoky Twelve line (matches the rule.tsv Smoky pattern, per the brief's own worked example). Added because Cadenhead's samples name it.
No peat mention found on Wikipedia; treated at the Highland default. Added because Cadenhead's samples name it.
Built for the J&B blend; no peat mention found, treated at the Speyside default. Added because Cadenhead's samples name it.

Core range (DoubleWood, 12/14/21 etc.) is unpeated; the distillery has released occasional peated limited editions (The Week of Peat, 14 Year Old Peat Week, Peated Cask 17 Year Old) not seen in this batch's samples, flag if such a name appears elsewhere. Added as parent of Burnside.

Well-documented teaspoon name Cadenhead uses for undisclosed Balvenie (per this project's research brief). Peat inferred from parent Balvenie's core unpeated range since no source names Burnside specifically; short/generic English word so alias scope is brand not any.
Added because Mossburn's Vintage Casks samples name it.
Added because Mossburn's Vintage Casks samples name it.
Added because Mossburn's Vintage Casks samples name it.
Main malt component of Chivas Regal; unpeated Speyside default. Added because Darkness!'s samples name it.

Peat level per the brief's own worked example (Bowmore listed alongside Talisker/Highland Park as medium); the fetched Wikipedia distillery page confirms identity/ownership but does not itself state a peat/ppm figure. Added because Darkness!'s samples name it.
Added because Darkness!'s samples name it.

Family-owned Kentucky distiller since 1935 (Bardstown/Louisville); Pikesville and Rittenhouse are its rye brands, range spans several types so defaultTypeName left empty. Added as parent of Pikesville.
